title: How To Be A Role Model For Your Students (And Not An Internet Troll)
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lays out eight behaviors that make a teacher into a genuine role model rather than a source of negativity students quietly mimic. His list ranges from living out a positive, solution-focused attitude instead of complaining publicly, to always following through on stated consequences so students can trust the teacher's word, to keeping personal struggles and opinions out of the classroom entirely. He stresses that students are constantly watching — noticing favoritism, phone-checking, and tone — far more than they listen to what's said, making consistent, professional behavior the real lever of influence. The piece closes with a pointed defense of SCM's approach and a warning against public negativity toward the site, tying personal integrity directly to the broader argument that teachers who want respect must first model the behavior they're asking students to display.
points: Publicly complaining or leaving negative comments undermines a teacher's ability to see the best in students and be respected by them.
Consistently following through on the classroom management plan is what earns a teacher students' trust; failing to do so erodes it.
Keeping personal opinions, politics, and struggles out of the classroom is framed as a professional obligation, not a suppression of personality.
Students notice everything — favoritism, tone, phone use, tardiness — far more than they absorb what a teacher explicitly says.
Cutting the amount of teacher talk by about a third is recommended to sharpen listening, work habits, and lesson clarity.
quotes: If you say you’re going to follow through on your classroom management plan and you don’t do it, then your students won’t trust you.
Consistency in word and deed is rare, but it will make you stick out like a flower among thorns.
It’s not about your politics. It’s not about your wants and needs. It’s not about the difficulties in your life, your future goals, or your stressful morning. Be a pro and keep them to yourself.
They notice how you treat others. They notice if you play favorites and the subtle way in which you smile at some but not others.
There are so few role models in this day and age that students will bend over backward to be around and please the real thing.
